synthetic_data.required_document_statement: Synthetic educational data created for NLP workshop purposes.
synthetic_data.required_institution_disclaimer: Hindu College of Engineering is a completely fictional educational institution created only for this workshop.
synthetic_data.provenance: Original synthetic design; no real institution policies, curricula, branding or faculty identities are used.
generation_rules: Reuse this contract for all in-scope academic facts; never invent conflicting facts in documents.
Include the exact required statement and explicitly describe the institution as fictional in every generated academic document and question paper.
Add any new in-scope fact to this contract and validate it before document generation.
Use references for policy values instead of maintaining independent copies.
Do not infer actual question-paper results from target counts before papers exist.

location.setting: Entirely invented teaching location; not a real town, district or campus address.

program.name: B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering
program.curriculum_scope: Compact complete workshop curriculum; not an accreditation claim.
program.elective_rule: Listed electives are the fixed choices in this synthetic cohort; no alternative elective catalog is implied.

courses.name: Programming Fundamentals
courses.description: Procedural programming develops step-by-step solutions using variables, decisions, repetition and functions, with attention to tracing and debugging small programs.

courses.name: Object-Oriented Programming
courses.description: Object-based software design organizes state and behaviour into classes, exploring encapsulation, inheritance and reusable abstractions for structured applications.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics
courses.description: Mathematical structures for computing connect logic, sets, relations and graph reasoning to precise statements about finite computational problems.

courses.name: Data Structures
courses.description: Organizing collections through lists, stacks, queues, trees and related structures supports efficient storage, access and modification of program data.

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.description: Relational data organization uses schemas, structured queries and integrity constraints to store linked records and maintain consistent information during updates.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Mathematical treatment of uncertainty combines probability distributions, summary statistics and inference to interpret variable observations and reason about evidence.

courses.name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
courses.description: Systematic algorithm design compares strategies for solving computational problems and evaluates their resource costs as input sizes change.

courses.name: Operating Systems
courses.description: System software coordinates processes, memory and shared resources so concurrent programs can run safely while using underlying computing hardware.

courses.name: Computer Networks
courses.description: Protocols and layered architectures that enable digital devices to exchange data over connected systems.

courses.name: Software Engineering
courses.description: Disciplined software development connects requirements, design, testing and maintenance to the construction of dependable applications by collaborating teams.

courses.name: Linear Algebra for Computing
courses.description: Vector spaces, matrices and linear transformations provide mathematical tools for representing numerical observations and reasoning about computations in multiple dimensions.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Intelligent problem solving examines search, knowledge representation and reasoning methods for choosing actions under specified goals and constraints.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Data-driven methods that learn patterns from examples to make predictions on unseen observations.
learning_objectives: Train and evaluate predictive models with suitable metrics.
Explain feature preparation and model validation.

courses.name: Data Engineering
courses.description: Data preparation workflows organize, clean and transform collections into dependable inputs for downstream analytical systems, emphasizing consistency across processing stages.

courses.name: Compiler Design
courses.description: Translation of programming languages connects lexical analysis, syntax and semantic checking to the construction of representations suitable for execution.

courses.name: Information Retrieval
courses.description: Retrieval of relevant items from document collections examines representations, ranking and evaluation, linking information needs with indexed textual evidence.

courses.name: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Computational methods for processing, understanding and generating human language through symbolic, statistical and contextual representations.
learning_objectives: Prepare text and explain representation choices.
Construct count-based and weighted language representations.
Explain sequence context, attention and Transformer representations.
Evaluate semantic similarity and retrieval experiments.

courses.name: Deep Learning
courses.description: Multilayer neural methods for learning hierarchical representations from data, building on Machine Learning.
learning_objectives: Train neural networks and diagnose generalization issues.
Compare convolutional, recurrent and attention-based architectures.

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.description: Visual pattern interpretation applies learned representations to images, considering recognition tasks and evaluation of predictions from visual observations.

courses.name: Distributed Systems
courses.description: Cooperating processes across multiple machines coordinate computation while reasoning about communication, consistency and failures in shared systems.

faculty_assignment_scope: Only the relevant AI/NLP and selected retrieval-teaching courses are assigned faculty. Empty faculty_ids mean unspecified, not unstaffed.

attendance_policy.scope: Each enrolled course separately, including laboratories, projects and seminars.
attendance_policy.measurement: Attended scheduled sessions divided by held scheduled sessions, multiplied by 100; compare the unrounded percentage with the threshold.
attendance_policy.shortage_definition: Attendance below minimum_percent in a course.
attendance_policy.shortage_consequence: Ineligible for that course's end-semester evaluation; internal marks alone do not waive the requirement.
attendance_policy.absence_rule: Approved leave does not automatically count as attended sessions. Students may request correction of an attendance recording error; verified corrections change the record, not the threshold.
attendance_policy.recovery: Re-enroll in the affected course at its next offering and meet the same attendance rule.

course_standard.pass_rule: Meet both minimum_total_to_pass and minimum_end_semester_to_pass; attendance eligibility is also required.

evaluation_modes.theory: Written midterm, coursework and written end-semester examination.
evaluation_modes.laboratory: Midterm practical and continuous records/experiments; end-semester practical demonstration and viva.
evaluation_modes.practical: Midterm progress review and continuous portfolio; end-semester project or seminar demonstration and viva.

examination.failed_course_rule: An eligible student failing either pass condition may take a reassessment at the next announced opportunity; its date is not defined in this calendar.

grading.basis: Absolute grading by total marks, after both pass conditions are met.
grading.marks_precision: Final marks are recorded as whole numbers.
grading.gpa_rule: Credit-weighted mean of grade points; F contributes zero. NE withholds the semester GPA until the course is completed.

academic_calendar.scope: One academic year across concurrent cohorts; odd and even semesters run together by parity, not sequentially within one year.
academic_calendar.scheduling_rule: Only explicitly listed course dates are fixed. Other course examinations fall within the relevant term window; exact dates remain unspecified.

laboratory_policy.attendance_rule: Identical to the general per-course attendance rule; no separate laboratory threshold.
laboratory_policy.record_submission: Submit a dated record for each assigned experiment, including inputs, method, observations and conclusion, by the term's records milestone.
laboratory_policy.experiment_completion: Complete every assigned experiment before the end-semester practical; the experiment list will be defined in later laboratory documents.
laboratory_policy.demonstration: Demonstrate working results and explain the method during the practical viva; project labs also demonstrate their final artifact.
laboratory_policy.missing_work_rule: Incomplete records or experiments affect continuous coursework marks; they do not introduce a separate examination eligibility threshold.
safety_and_discipline: Use only instructor-approved datasets and software.
Do not share passwords or include personal data in experiments.
Handle equipment responsibly and report faults.
Acknowledge collaboration and submit your own explanation of results.

placement_policy.scope: Fictional institution-level preparation and recruitment registration only; no employer-specific claims.
placement_policy.preparation_registration: Students in Semesters 5 through 8 may register for placement preparation, including students with pending courses.
placement_policy.guarantee: Preparation or eligibility does not guarantee an interview, internship or job.

question_paper_design.counting_unit: One primary topic per top-level question slot; no sub-question double counting. Secondary related topics may be annotated but do not count toward these targets.
question_paper_design.assessment_scope: Generated papers represent the 60-mark end-semester component: twelve compulsory five-mark top-level questions per paper.
question_paper_design.alias_rule: Aliases are retrieval/matching cues, not guaranteed exact equivalents. Resolve overlap with context and assign one primary topic; Word2Vec, CBOW and Skip-Gram remain distinct taxonomy IDs.
question_paper_design.validation_rule: Future generated papers must match the per-paper primary-topic counts and be validated against actual annotated questions. Targets are design intent, not historical results.

retrieval_design.reference_convention: course IDs are canonical course codes; topic IDs are taxonomy IDs; fact IDs are RFC 6901 JSON pointers into this file. Expected references identify facts, not generated document IDs.
retrieval_design.evaluation_rule: Once documents exist, assign source IDs, verify support for each reference and record lexical/semantic rankings. Semantic contrast is a teaching hypothesis, not a promised ranking improvement.

benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Retrieve the single canonical attendance threshold.

benchmarks.query: Find the TF-IDF unit in the NLP syllabus.
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Establish an exact-term lexical retrieval baseline.

benchmarks.query: Which subject teaches computers to interpret human language?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Retrieve the language-focused course from a paraphrased description.
benchmarks.source_phrasing_hint: Use the canonical NLP description about computational methods for processing, understanding and generating human language; do not copy the query.
benchmarks.semantic_rationale: The query paraphrases the canonical concept using different terminology. Compare lexical rankings with semantic rankings; neither method is guaranteed to win.

benchmarks.query: How much classroom presence do I need to sit my finals?

benchmarks.source_phrasing_hint: Describe attendance and end-semester examination eligibility using the canonical policy; keep the percentage numeric in the contract.
benchmarks.semantic_rationale: The query paraphrases the canonical concept using different terminology. Compare lexical rankings with semantic rankings; neither method is guaranteed to win.

benchmarks.query: Which class learns to predict outcomes from examples?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Retrieve Machine Learning without the course title in the query.
benchmarks.source_phrasing_hint: Use the Machine Learning description: data-driven methods, patterns and unseen observations.
benchmarks.semantic_rationale: The query paraphrases the canonical concept using different terminology. Compare lexical rankings with semantic rankings; neither method is guaranteed to win.

benchmarks.source_phrasing_hint: Use the Computer Networks description about protocols, layered architectures and exchanging data; avoid query wording.
benchmarks.semantic_rationale: The query paraphrases the canonical concept using different terminology. Compare lexical rankings with semantic rankings; neither method is guaranteed to win.

benchmarks.query: What should I study before taking Deep Learning?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Return all prerequisites, including Machine Learning and Linear Algebra for Computing.

benchmarks.query: How do Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing differ?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Compare broad predictive learning with language-focused methods using both course descriptions.

benchmarks.query: When is the NLP examination and what topics are included?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Combine the specific NLP examination date with its five syllabus units.
Map Semester 6 to the even-semester term.

benchmarks.query: When are laboratory examinations for Semester 6?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Retrieve a date range rather than inventing an individual lab date.

benchmarks.query: How is an NLP course evaluated and what is required to pass?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Explain component weights and both pass conditions.

benchmarks.query: Summarize what I must submit and demonstrate in a laboratory.
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Summarize several requirements without introducing extra conditions.

benchmarks.query: Which NLP topics appeared most frequently in previous examinations?
benchmarks.teaching_purpose: After papers are generated, compute actual counts and compare with targets. Targets alone are not observed historical evidence.

benchmarks.teaching_purpose: Distinguish preparation access from recruitment eligibility.
